newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian opposition threatens boycott of vote.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition threatens boycott of vote.

text.p: Serbian opposition parties said on Friday they would boycott upcoming federal elections if the government refused to appoint their representatives to electoral boards supervising the vote.

The five-party coalition running in rump Yugoslavia's federal and local elections on November 3 accused the government of trying to retain exclusive control over the electoral commissions which count ballots and supervise voting.

"If participation of our members is not assured in the electoral boards during vote counting we will consider the elections illegal and we will not participate in these elections," Zoran Djindjic, head of the Democratic Party, told a news conference in Belgrade.
The electoral boards in districts across Serbia and Montenegro would be named in the next few days and the "Together" coalition would then decide whether to stage a boycott, he said.

"Under these conditions there is absolutely no sense in taking part in the elections and those who make decisions will be responsible for any consequences of our boycotting the elections," Djindjic said.
The opposition leaders said they entered the campaign fully aware they woul d be denied free access to state media but could not accept the ruling party controlling the electoral boards.
"This is the minimum below which we cannot go," he added.

The "Together" coalition, which covers a political spectrum from liberal to rightwing nationalist, has been scoring well in opinion polls against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, who keeps tight control over media and police.

The opposition parties, which are calling for democratic and free-market reforms, have managed to overcome deep political differences and present a unified front for the first time, attracting large crowds at many of their rallies.
Opposition leaders alleged that a ruling party official in Nis had told them opposition members would be kicked off of electoral boards.
There was no immediate response from the Belgrade government to the allegations.
